# 1 Clement Chapter 6 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_006_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 6

**6:1** To these men who pursued a holy way of life was added a great multitude of the elect, who through many indignities and tortures — suffering these things because of jealousy — set among us a most excellent example.

**6:2** Because of jealousy women were persecuted — as Danaids and Dirces — and having endured terrible and unholy outrages, they ran safely the race of faith and received a noble prize, though weak in body.

**6:3** Jealousy has estranged wives from their husbands, and perverted the word of our father Adam: "This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh." [Gen 2:23]

**6:4** Jealousy and strife have overthrown great cities and uprooted mighty nations.

---

*LOGOS notes: "Danaids and Dirces" are mythological figures whose punishment-roles were apparently assigned to Christian martyrs in theatrical executions under Nero (cf. Tacitus, Annals 15.44). The LXX quotation in 6:3 is exact.*
